title: Conditional knockdown protocol for studying cellular communication using Drosophila melanogaster wing imaginal disc
protocol: Obtain female flies with the genotype Krlf-1/CyO; GAL80ts/Tm6B, Tb.
Cross female virgin flies with the genotype Krlf-1/CyO; +/Tm6B, Tb with male flies of genotype +/CyO; tubP-GAL80ts to establish host stock.
Obtain flies with the genotype ex-lacZ, ptc-GAL4, UAS-EGFP/CyO; tubP-GAL80ts/Tm6B, Sb Tb.
Cross virgin female flies with the genotype Krlf-1/CyO; tubP-GAL80ts/Tm6B, Tb with male flies of the genotype ex-lacZ, ptc-GAL4, UAS-EGFP/CyO; +/Tm6B, Sb Tb.
Discard offspring displaying the Krlf-1 phenotype characterized by abnormal eye appearance.
Select virgin female and male offspring with the genotype ex-lacZ, ptc-GAL4, UAS-EGFP/Cyo; tubP-GAL80ts/Tm6B, Sb Tb for maintenance as host stock.
Cross selected offspring (ex-lacZ, ptc-GAL4, UAS-EGFP/Cyo; tubP-GAL80ts/Tm6B, Sb Tb) with a fly stock known to exhibit a strong phenotype.
Observe the resulting progeny for any strong wing phenotype indicating the presence of tubP-GAL80ts on the third chromosome.
Cross female virgin flies with the genotype ex-lacZ, ptc-GAL4, UAS-EGFP/CyO; tubP-GAL80ts/Tm6B, Sb Tb with UAS-scrib RNAi male flies.
Pick larvae that are GFP positive and without Tm6B, Sb Tb balancers from scrib RNAi flies.
Cross female virgin flies with the genotype ex-lacZ, ptc-GAL4, UAS-EGFP/Cyo; tubP-GAL80ts/Tm6B, Sb Tb with UAS-mCherry RNAi male flies.
Ensure collected females exhibit phenotypic characteristics of virgins such as presence of meconium on the abdomen, unfolded wings, or clear and swollen abdomen.
Collect virgin females within 4–6 hours after hatching from pupal case for maximum accuracy.
Add yeast to vials prior to initiating crosses to enhance nutrient availability and increase offspring yield.
Cross female flies with UAS-mCherry RNAi male flies.
Place the male and female adult flies together in a fresh vial.
Incubate the vial containing the flies at 25 degrees for 24 hours.
Maintain flies at 25°C for 24 hours to promote optimal conditions for egg laying.
Transfer vials containing embryos to RT (21°C) for 3 days.
Shift the vials to a 29°C incubator for 2–4 days after 3 days.
Collect late 3rd instar larvae 2–4 days following the temperature shift.
After 24 hours, transfer adult flies to another new vial.
Place vials containing fertilized eggs at 21 degrees for 3 days.
Transfer vials to a 29-degree incubator for a period of 2–4 days.
Maintain consistent timing throughout all steps.
Synchronize temperatures and starting time points across all collected samples to ensure larvae are at a similar developmental stage.
Start all steps at the same time of the day for synchronization.
Establish three separate vials of the same host stock in parallel for each time point in a given experiment.
Obtain samples from multiple vials at different time points within the 2–4 day period.
Dissect samples.
Fix samples in 37% formaldehyde.
Stain samples as required.
Mount samples on glass bottom dishes for imaging.
Prepare all necessary materials and equipment for dissection and fixation, including sample larvae, forceps, pipettes, and Eppendorf tubes.
Position the larva on a silicon or glass plate.
Remove roughly one-third of the posterior end of the larva.
Expose the wing discs located on the anterior part of the larva.
Use a permanent marker to label microscope slides.
Prepare cavity well microscope slides using 70% ethanol and Kim Wipes for cleaning.
Mount the sample on a superfrost microscope slide with transparent tape.
Apply commercial mounting solution or 70% glycerol in 1× PBS to the slide.
Place the wing disc onto the mounted slide using forceps.
Secure the cover slip over the sample using transparent nail polish.
Label each prepared slide carefully.
Use a positively charged microscope slide to facilitate proper sample adhesion.
Position a piece of tape at the center of the slide ensuring it adheres securely.
Use a scalpel to create a gap in the center area of the tape providing a defined area for the sample.
After adding the mounting solution, seal the cover glass with transparent nail polish.
Carefully collect larvae displaying the desired phenotype and transfer them into a glass bottom dish containing 1× Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Place the glass bottom dish with larvae onto a bed of ice to minimize mobility and slow developmental processes.
Gently transfer the larvae from the container onto a puddle of 1× PBS on a glass or silicone plate.
Utilize the “Opening the window” technique as the initial dissection approach for the larvae.
Use forceps to carefully remove approximately one-third of the posterior end of the larvae.
Gently expose the wing discs located on the anterior part of the larvae using forceps.
Carefully transfer the anterior part of the larvae, containing the exposed wing discs, into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 1×PBS.
Place Eppendorf tubes containing wing discs on ice.
Prepare a 3.7% formaldehyde (FA) solution by mixing 900 μL of 1×PBT with 100 μL of 37% FA in a separate tube.
Remove 1× PBS from the tube containing exposed wing discs.
Add prepared FA solution to the tube containing exposed wing discs.
Incubate tube with FA solution at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Carefully remove FA solution from the tube without disrupting wing discs.
Wash sample by performing three consecutive washes, each lasting 5 minutes, using 1×PBT.
Transfer the anterior part of the larvae containing exposed wing discs to a puddle of 1× PBS on a glass or silicone plate.
Dissect one wing disc from each larva carefully.
Collect dissected wing discs and transfer them to an Eppendorf tube containing 1× PBT.
Perform three consecutive washes by immersing the samples in 1× PBT for 10 minutes each time.
Allow sufficient time (10 minutes) between washes for the wing discs to settle at the bottom of the Eppendorf tube.
Leave the washed wing discs in 1× PBT for an additional 15 minutes.
Prepare a blocking buffer by mixing 95 μL of 1× PBT with 5 μL of normal goat serum (NGS).
Remove 1× PBT from the tube containing washed wing discs.
Add the BB solution to the sample.
Incubate the BB at RT for 1 h.
Remove the BB solution from the sample.
Prepare the antibody (AB) solution by diluting the desired primary AB(s).
Ensure a final volume of 100 μL containing 5 μL of NGS and 95 μL of 1×PBT.
Add the primary AB solution to the tube containing the wing discs.
Incubate overnight at 4 degrees for primary AB staining.
Gently remove the primary AB staining from the wing discs.
Perform three consecutive 10-min washes using 1× PBT at RT.
Prepare the AB solution by diluting the desired secondary antibodies (1:200) in an Eppendorf tube, ensuring a final volume of 100 μL.
Include 5 μL of NGS and 95 μL of 1×PBT in the AB solution.
Remove excess primary antibody solution from the sample by washing with 1×PBT.
Add the secondary AB solution to the sample containing the wing discs.
Incubate the secondary AB solution for 2 h at room temperature (RT).
Mounting of the sample(s) should be done in the dark.
Prepare a positively charged microscopy slide.
Place a piece of tape at the center of the microscopy slide.
Use a scalpel to carefully create a gap in the center portion of the tape.
Clean the designated sample area on the slide using a Kimwipe sprayed with 70% ethanol.
Mount the sample on the slide.
Transfer wings from Eppendorf tube onto a separate glass or silicone plate using a 20-200 μL pipette.
Employ careful pipetting technique to ensure precise and delicate transfer of wing samples, avoiding excess liquid transfer.
Carefully transfer the wings onto the gap of the microscopy slide.
Remove any excess liquid from the sample using a Kimwipe.
Alternatively, use a pipette to suction up extra liquid.
Add a drop of mounting solution to the center of the sample.
Use either commercial mounting solution or prepare 70% glycerol in 1×PBS.
Ensure pH is correct (optimal 7.5) if using 70% glycerol as mounting solution.
Place cover glass over the sample using forceps, touching one edge to the slide first and then slowly lowering the other edge.
Seal edges of the cover glass with transparent nail polish to secure it in place.
Subject the prepared slides to imaging using a confocal microscope.
Select excitation wavelengths based on the absorption and fluorescent proteins used.
Determine the appropriate zoom level for imaging the wings.
Use a 20× zoom objective for imaging the entire wing disc.
Use a 60×/90× zoom objective for imaging at the (sub)-cellular level.
Utilize Z-stack imaging to capture multiple images on different focal planes along the Z-axis.
Set the starting point for the Z-stack to cover the beginning of the Z-axis of the wing imaginal disc.
Set the end point for the Z-stack to cover the entire vertical axis of the wing imaginal disc.
Drag the confocal image into ImageJ/Fiji.
Select Split channels.
Navigate to Image menu, select Color, and choose Merge Channels.
Verify the appropriate starting and ending points for Z-stacks before proceeding with compression.
Select desired slices within the Image menu, under the Stacks option, and choose Z-Project.
Specify the starting and stopping slices for compression.
Save the image.
Navigate to the File menu within ImageJ/Fiji.
Choose a suitable file format, suggesting TIFF.
Specify the desired file name.
Start a new document in CorelDRAW.
Specify the desired width and height for the document.
Import the image into CorelDRAW.
Select the Freehand tool from the left-hand panel.
Draw the line along the GFP expression region using the Freehand tool.
Set the desired outline width for the drawn line.
Select a suitable line style for the drawn line.
Modify the drawn line further by selecting the Shape option in the left-hand panel.
Choose a color that effectively highlights the GFP expression region from the available options in the right-side panel.
Set the desired outline width.
Choose a line style to customize the appearance of the line.
Trace and mark the GFP-positive area by drawing a line.
Select the Shape option in the left-hand panel to modify the drawn line.
Add curves or alter the shape as needed.
Choose the desired color for the line from the options provided in the right-hand panel.
Save the image.
Navigate to the File menu, choose the Save as option.
Save the image with the marked GFP-positive area.
Phalloidin selectively binds to F-actin for visualization of cytoskeletal organization, cell shapes, and wing epithelial sheet integrity.
DAPI preferentially binds to AT-rich regions of DNA for visualization of cell nuclei location and morphology within the wing disc.
